title: Security finding — possible pull_request_target pattern (details on request)
description:
Hi 👋

Automated scan from [Lictor](https://lictor-ai.com) flagged a `pull_request_target` workflow that checks out the PR head SHA/ref. That's the *pattern* of the classic GitHub Actions RCE — but exploitability depends on your guards. I verified the pattern, **not** exploitability.

- **What I saw:** `pull_request_target` + a checkout step referencing the head ref.
- **Why it might matter:** without label gates / approved-ci / fork-PR filters, fork PRs can run with write-scoped tokens.
- **What to check:** the workflow file the scan flagged. If your guards are sufficient (label requirement, dependabot-only, head.repo.full_name check, etc.), this is a non-issue — close out and a quick note helps me tune the scanner. For the exact file/line, reply here or email **Raffa@Lictor-AI.com**.

Either way — thank you for the work you do on this repo. 🙏

— Raffa · Lictor (open-source, Apache 2.0)

title: vetiver_write_plumber not generating board code correctly for board_databricks
description:
Hello,

I am building out an ML workflow using the `targets` package. In it, I am aiming to accomplish the following:

1. Generate training data and train model
2. Assess the training accuracy against the champion model
3. If the new model is better, save the vetiver model as a pin in Databricks
4. If the new model is better, auto deploy the model pin (stored in Databricks) on Posit Connect as an API

Vetiver seems to do most of this correctly, but I'm running into an interesting issue in the `vetiver_write_plumber` function. It appears that for a databricks_board object (I haven't tested other board locations), the code to generate the board reference does not work as intended. Looking at the deployed plumber file, I get the following snippet of code in the file for the board reference:

c("b <- board_databricks(folder_url = \"<URL>", host = \"<REDACTED>",", "b <-   prefix = \"<PREFIX>\", versioned = TRUE, cache = \"./\")")
v <- vetiver_pin_read(b, "<MODEL_NAME>", version = "<VERSION>")

As you can see, it's a vector with multiple assignments to b, rather than just one assignment.
The code currently in `vetiver_write_plumber` is the following:

```## rlang::expr_deparse won't work for board_url, but
  ## base deparse won't work for S3 and other complex boards:
  if (inherits(board, "pins_board_url")) {
    board <- deparse(pins::board_deparse(board))
  } else {
    board <- rlang::expr_deparse(pins::board_deparse(board))
  }
  board <- glue('b <- {board}')
```

I made a local version of this function and instead replaced it with:
```
## Always deparse to a single scalar string
  ## board_deparse() returns a call object (language), not credentials.
  call_obj <- pins::board_deparse(board)  
  
  if (inherits(board, "pins_board_url")) {
    # base::deparse() returns a character vector -> collapse explicitly
    board_str <- paste(base::deparse(call_obj), collapse = " ")
  } else {
    # rlang ensures a single string representation of the expression
    board_str <- rlang::expr_text(call_obj) 
  }
  # Now 'board_str' is one line; safe to put inside glue:
  board_line <- glue::glue('b <- {board_str}')
```

This seemed to do the trick, and it writes the board reference correctly. Figured I would write it here in case others have run into this issue as well

title: `vetiver_pr_docs(all_docs = FALSE)` doesn't generate docs for the `predict` endpoint
description:
I have a plumber API generated by `vetiver` where I would like to have additional POST endpoints that don't inherit the auto-documentation that `vetiver` applies to the `predict` endpoint. I thought this could be achieved by setting `vetiver_pr_docs(all_docs = FALSE)` but this causes no documentation to be generated for the `predict` endpoint.

## Reprex

```r
library(vetiver)

cars_lm <- lm(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)
v <- vetiver_model(cars_lm, "cars_linear")

library(plumber)

# Docs for predict endpoint aren't generated
pr() |>
  vetiver_pr_post(v) |>
  vetiver_pr_docs(v, all_docs = FALSE) |>
  pr_post("/test", \() "test", description = "TEST") |>
  pr_run()

# Docs for test endpoint are overwritten
pr() |>
  vetiver_pr_post(v) |>
  vetiver_pr_docs(v, all_docs = TRUE) |>
  pr_post("/test", \() "test", description = "TEST") |>
  pr_run()
```

## Ideal Solution

`vetiver_pr_docs(all_docs = FALSE)` autogenerates docs for the `predict` endpoint but leaves other POST endpoints untouched.

title: Allow Custom Models to Assign Packages
description:
## Background

This issue is in reference to the discussion had on #214.

Our team has a custom package responsible for making a model, and we want to set up and deploy a vetiver API endpoint from that same package. When working with the custom model wrapped by `vetiver_model()`, we had difficulty getting our deployed API on Posit Connect to correctly find the new methods we had made (i.e. `handler_predict.my_model`, etc.) and would get the error:

```
There is no method available to build a prediction handler for `x`.
```

## Current Output

Indicating those methods weren't being carried over. The default output file for `vetiver::vetiver_write_plumber()` looks something like:

```r
# Generated by the vetiver package; edit with care

library(pins)
library(plumber)
library(rapidoc)
library(vetiver)

# Packages needed to generate model predictions
if (FALSE) {
    library(myCustomPackage)
    library(otherusefulpackages)
    ...
}
b <- board_connect(auth = "envvar")
v <- vetiver_pin_read(b, "my_model")

#* @plumber
function(pr) {
    pr %>% vetiver_api(v)
}

```

What we found worked was moving the `library()` call for the custom package out of `if (FALSE) { }`. Then the deployed API correctly picked up the custom methods for our model.

## Proposed Solution

It might be helpful to allow users to edit what packages are attached to the default plumber output, currently they are rigidly set in `infra_pkgs`:

https://github.com/rstudio/vetiver-r/blob/581a4e98d9673013a386a9715f180f025fc3f03f/R/write-plumber.R#L96

title: Saving `lm` model via vetiver object takes a lot of space
description:
Hi,

Thank you for putting effort into trying to make live easier for ML people. :)
I am just experimenting with the `vetiver` package to see if we can make use of it, and am stumbling over some issues.

I set up a simple tidymodels workflow, fitted some data (~ 14 mio records), created a vetiver object and tried to persist it with `vetiver_pin_write()`.
The problem I have is that the result takes ~ 1.4 GB on my hard disk.

Is this intentional? In our use case we really only need the (stored) model to make predictions and provide confidence intervals. For that storing the training coefficients and associated uncertainties should be enough, and I don't see why that should take 1.4 GB of space.

I tried to experiment with the `model = FALSE` parameter for `lm()`, but that only reduced the filesize by half or so. It seems it has something to do with some fit$qr$qr object inside the fit model. I can manually remove that, and the filesize gets to an acceptible size, but neither `vetiver` nor `butcher` do so automatically.

Do I have to live with the fact that the trained models will take a big amount of space or are there some measures I can take to get it to a size of the order of a couple of KB?

title: Support for serverless inference and multi-model endpoints on sagemaker
description:
Hi there! I was wondering if either of these two things have been discussed or brought up as potential additions to the development  roadmap.

And I think multi-model endpoints are a solution to the need to have multiple models, as having a constantly running endpoint for every model would be so expensive. But this requires changing the docker file a bit from my understanding. So that may be something to handle in the sm-docker package.

Besides multi-model endpoints, is there any existing strategy for deploying on the order of ~100 different vetiver models to sagemaker? Or anywhere else for that matter - with emphasis on low cost / low memory while potentially giving up some good latency.

description:
Hello,

I've been developing a few models and have been able to deploy all of them to Posit Connect successfully. The documentation on all of this is very clear so a quick thanks to those who worked on it! :)

Having said that, I'm having trouble actually making predictions once the model has been deployed onto the server.

```

v <- vetiver_model(final_fit_to_deploy, model_name = "SOME_NAME")
```

`endpoint<- vetiver_endpoint("https://connect.COMPANY.com/PAGENAME/predict")`

title: Consider adding support for apptainer/singularity
description:
We already have support for [generating Dockerfiles plus needed artifacts](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-r/reference/vetiver_prepare_docker.html) for serving vetiver models. Let's consider also adding support for [Apptainer/Singularity](https://apptainer.org/) containers. Apptainer/Singularity is different from Docker in that a data scientist could build and run a container completely in user space (without admin or close to admin privileges); this may be a better option for more constrained computational environments. I notice the [rang](https://github.com/chainsawriot/rang) package has support for both and would be worth checking out in more detail.

title: Support for out-of-distribution detection with one class SVMs
description:
One use case for vetiver would be monitoring whether new data that the model encounters in real world belongs to the same distribution of data seen during model training, or whether there is a covariate shift over time. I wonder if this would be a useful addition to vetiver. 

We could potentially use one-class support vector machines for novelty detection, as proposed by [Schölkopf et al](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/1999/hash/8725fb777f25776ffa9076e44fcfd776-Abstract.html). The idea is to define a frontier boundary surface around the training points in the p-dimensional feature space and check to see if new observations fall within or outside this frontier. Schölkopf et al suggest a single-class SVF to find the tightest hypersphere around the data. Probabilistic outputs from one-class SVMs can quantify the probability that the newly-observed data belongs to the distribution of training data.

In terms of implementation, [LIBSVM](https://www.csie.ntu.edu.tw/~cjlin/libsvm/) provides the go-to implementation of one-class SVMs, and since version 3.31 (Feb. 2023) supports probabilistic outputs for one-class SVMs. 

For vetiver-python, we could potentially use [libsvm-official](https://pypi.org/project/libsvm-official/), which supports one-class probabilistic outputs. There is also [sklearn.svm.OneClassSVM](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.svm.OneClassSVM.html) which seems to be a separate implementation inspired by libsvm, but I am not sure if it supports probabilistic outcomes. 

For vetiver-r,  the [e1071 ](https://cran.r-project.org/package=e1071) package provides an interface to LIBSVM but currently supports LIBSVM 3.23, which does not include probabilistic outputs. Another possibility is to use [kernlab ](https://cran.r-project.org/package=kernlab) with `type="one-svc"`, but to the best of my knowledge, kernlab does not produce probabilistic outcomes, and current predictions with one-class SVM with kernlab and tidymodels is buggy: https://github.com/tidymodels/parsnip/issues/974

What do you think @juliasilge?

title: Allow vetiver_write_docker to change base image
description:
vetiver_write_docker should be allowed to change the base image. This is down to AWS CodeBuild throttling dockerhub.

```
toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit. You may increase the limit by authenticating and upgrading: https://www.docker.com/increase-rate-limit
```

This is a fairly common issue https://github.com/aws-samples/sagemaker-studio-image-build-cli/issues/26 and to allow customer base images (i.e. ecr repository for AWS CodeBuild) should fix this. 

For example something like this:

```r
vetiver_write_docker <- function(vetiver_model,
                                 plumber_file = "plumber.R",
                                 path = ".",
                                 lockfile = "vetiver_renv.lock",
                                 rspm = TRUE,
                                 docker_from = default_base_image(),
                                 port = 8000,
                                 expose = TRUE,
                                 additional_pkgs = character(0)) {
  from_r_version <- docker_from
  rspm_env <- ifelse(rspm, "ENV RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/latest\n",
    ""
  )
  pkgs <- unique(c(additional_pkgs, docker_pkgs, vetiver_model$metadata$required_pkgs))
  pkgs <- setdiff(pkgs, drop_pkgs)
  lockfile_pkgs <- renv$snapshot(
    project = path, lockfile = lockfile,
    packages = pkgs, prompt = FALSE, force = TRUE
  )
  plumber_file <- fs::path_rel(plumber_file)
  sys_reqs <- glue_sys_reqs(names(lockfile_pkgs$Packages))
  copy_renv <- glue("COPY {lockfile} renv.lock")
  copy_plumber <- glue("COPY {plumber_file} /opt/ml/plumber.R")
  expose <- ifelse(expose, glue("EXPOSE {port}"), "")
  entrypoint <- glue(
    "ENTRYPOINT [\"R\", \"-e\", ", "\"pr <- plumber::plumb('/opt/ml/plumber.R'); ",
    "pr$run(host = '0.0.0.0', port = {port})\"]"
  )
  ret <- compact(list(
    "# Generated by the vetiver package; edit with care\n",
    from_r_version, rspm_env, sys_reqs, "", copy_renv, "RUN Rscript -e \"install.packages('renv')\"",
    "RUN Rscript -e \"renv::restore()\"", copy_plumber, expose,
    entrypoint
  ))
  readr::write_lines(ret, file = file.path(path, "Dockerfile"))
}

default_base_image <- function() {
  glue::glue("FROM rocker/r-ver:{getRversion()}")
}
```

Linked ticket: https://github.com/rstudio/vetiver-r/issues/175

title: Using Vetiver for UMAPs
description:
Hi Posit team,

Thanks for your hard work on Vetiver - it looks like a very useful package that my team is looking at implementing for our supervised ML models.

I was wondering if it's possible to use Vetiver with UMAP models - that is, to version the models and also to use the API to project new data into existing models. As an example, we often need to project new data into previously-created UMAPs, and eventually update the UMAPs using all the available data. At present we simply track versions of UMAPs using a date stamp in the filename of the saved model object, but it would be great to have a more effective solution.

Vetiver doesn't appear to support UMAP directly (we are working in R with the uwot package), so initially we thought we could use the tidymodels framework.

However (as far as I can tell) Vetiver requires from tidymodels a "workflow" object on which the predict function can be called. The workflow object comprises a "recipe" part and a "model" part. The UMAP step is contained in the "recipe" as a pre-processing step, rather than as a "model". As a result, I haven't been able to create a workflow that can use a predict function to transform new data into UMAP coordinates.

Do you have any suggestions for how we can work around this issue? If it's not possible now, is this something that the Posit team is considering adding to Vetiver in the future?

Thank you!

title: Refactor metadata, specifically move `required_pkgs`
description:
We've decided to keep as much metadata as possible outside of the binary bundle, stored in plain text (YAML). As of today, here is what is wrapped up into the binary object:

https://github.com/rstudio/vetiver-r/blob/8875142d10aff1d55dc16170725f114a629b2884/R/pin-read-write.R#L38-L40

In R, we don't have any tool like [pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/) that can completely/accurately store that can store the signature/schema/ptype of a dataframe in plain text like JSON or YAML. This means that for now, we will keep the `prototype` / `ptype` in the `list()` that gets serialized to binary when storing.

It is possible/easier to move `required_pkgs` to the `user` metadata slot, since it's just plain text.

title: vetiver_ptype gets congfused if lm has interaction terms
description:
I kept getting the following error when trying to make vetiver_model of a lm object, which I narrowed down to be an issue of ptype

> > vetiver_ptype(model)
> Error in `[.data.frame`(model$model, pred_names) : 
>   undefined columns selected

If I read the codebase correctly, it might be an issue of not taking out interaction terms of lm models before building the ptype resulting in the error. I'm not confident enough in the elegance of my solution to make a PR out of this, but have provided a solution that does seem to eliminate the error.

Minimal working example (with a possible way to fix the issue demonstrated)
```
library(vetiver)

data(mtcars)
model <- lm(mpg ~ cyl*gear+disp, data=mtcars)

# this does not work
vetiver_ptype(model)

# removing interaction terms from pred_names
vetiver_ptype_edited.lm <- function(model, ...) {
  pred_names <- attr(model$terms, "term.labels")
  # taking away interaction terms, they will always have a ':' in them
  pred_names_without_interaction <- pred_names[!grepl(':',pred_names)]
  ptype <- vctrs::vec_ptype(model$model[pred_names_without_interaction])
  tibble::as_tibble(ptype)
}

# this works
vetiver_ptype_edited.lm(model)
```

I understand if this is a route you don't want to go down, but there are situations where deploying *without* plumber makes sense, such as on AWS Lambda (see #128). It would be nice to avoid installing extra things in that case, and {plumber} comes with a number of dependencies, including {sodium}, which has a `libsodium` system requirement (and thus adds another step to the process).

Would you consider moving {plumber} to Suggests for {vetiver}, and only adding it to the `vetiver_renv.lock` when it makes sense to do so (ie, for almost every deployment path other than Lambda, probably)?

It probably isn't a HUGE issue, but I can imagine getting to a point where we want to shave every little thing out of that container that we can.

title: Consider changing error status to 422
description:
We could change the error that folks see on predicting with bad data from 400 to 422. This would involve doing something like this within `vetiver_pr_post()`:

```r
pr <- plumber::pr_set_error(pr, handler_error_422)
```

where `handler_error_422()` would be something like:

```r
handler_error_422 <- function(req, res, err) {
    res$status <- 422
    list(error = "422 - Unprocessable Entity", message = err$message)
}
```

One issue that I haven't resolved yet is that I think as I have this laid out ⬆️ this will change _all_ errors to 422, even ones that aren't predicting with valid but not endpoint-appropriate JSON. I would need to add more careful checking somehow.

This is motivated by FastAPI returning 422 in the situation where valid JSON is posted but it doesn't match the Pydantic model. @isabelizimm have I stated this correctly? Is this still the case? It do think it is a good idea to harmonize the error status codes between R and Python.

In [reading the spec for the 422 code](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/422) and [various discussions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16133923/400-vs-422-response-to-post-of-data), I'm not 100% sure that switching from 400 to 422 is best or right just based on what we're doing. Maybe we can get more feedback 400 vs. 422 for the context of model predictions?

title: Support deployment through AWS Lambda
description:
I'm following up on a tweet from a long time ago about implementing this. All the rstudio::conf tweets make me want to build something!

The end goal of this feature would be to simplify and automate the creation of a Dockerfile, the image of which can be deployed as an AWS Lambda function. Users could then access the model through any of the supported [AWS integrations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-services.html) (including a HTTP API Gateway). 

Like `vetiver_write_docker`, the goal is not to do the actual deployment and configuration of the endpoint, but to produce a Dockerfile that can be built into an image which is deployed:

| Deployment | First use...  | Then create a Dockerfile with... |
| :------------ | :--------------- | :------------------------------ |
|  Docker | `vetiver_write_plumber` | `vetiver_write_docker` |
| AWS Lambda | `vetiver_write_lambda_runtime` | `vetiver_write_lambda` |

If the maintainers are okay with this proposal I'm happy to implement this (with an unknown time frame!). The following changes would need to be made:

* introduce `lambdr` as a "Suggests" dependency.
* write the `vetiver_write_lambda_runtime` function with an API identical to that of `vetiver_write_plumber`. The generated runtime file would need to read the model pin, source packages, and then run some sort of `predict` function.
* create an internal `vetiver_write_dockerfile` function that would be used by both `vetiver_write_docker` and `vetiver_write_lambda`. This is so we can have more flexible options for writing Dockerfiles, especially using different parent images. [We're aiming for a Dockerfile like the one shown here](https://lambdr.mdneuzerling.com/articles/lambda-runtime-in-container.html).

title: Challenges when sharing models due to package versions
description:
I am currently sharing development models using the example workflow:

```r
library(vetiver)
library(pins)

# connect to model board
b <- board_s3(
  bucket = "models", 
  prefix = "label/", 
  region = structure("us-east-1", tags = list(type = "scalar"))
)

# checkout the version you want
v <- vetiver_pin_read(
  board = b, 
  name = "label", 
  version = "20220701T182136Z-9905d"
)

# create some dummy data
new_data <- data.frame(
  predictor = c(
    "some text",
    "more text"
  )
)

# occasionally, models require packages be loaded
load_pkgs(v$metadata$required_pkgs)
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'tune':
#>   method                   from   
#>   required_pkgs.model_spec parsnip

# make predictions
predict(v, new_data)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>   .pred_class
#>   <fct>      
#> 1 TRUE       
#> 2 FALSE
```

However, we have found that this doesn't always work due to package versions being different from computer to computer. Occasionally, a user will call `predict` on new data and an error is returned as a result of package version differences. We have come to this conclusion because some computers can run the exact same code without error.

Is there a suggested workflow or any guidance on how to share development models? We are thinking of making a function like `with_model_env` that would leverage the `renv.lock` to run the model with the same set of packages temporarily but wanted to see if there is a better approach.

title: For discussion: `ptype` naming convention could be confusing to python users
description:
I have had some exposure to both the Python and R vetiver packages. I want to start a discussion around the `ptype` parameter name (e.g. `save_ptype`, `ptype_data`, etc.). 

I think it could be confusing for python users. In pandas, there is the notion of [dtypes](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.dtypes.html). 

At first glance, I thought ptype was some how related. This is quickly cleared up if you read the docs... However, I think there could be some initial confusion for those who do not read the docs first.

Could it be reasonable to change the name to be more verbose? E.g. `save_prototype` and `prototype_data`? I think this would make it more clear that it is not related to types, and is instead related to prototypes. Going even one step further, is prototype the right word? When I think of prototypes I think of early / pre-release versions of a product.

title: Consider creating Plumber APIs with a `QUERY` endpoint in addition to `POST`
description:
## Background

At my previous job we served model predictions via Plumber APIs (with identical endpoint names, even). Originally these endpoints used `GET` requests, but eventually some models required arguments too long or complex to put into a query string, so we moved to using `POST` with the arguments in the body. The reason for this is that `GET` requests are not expected to have a body, and many programs or intermediate proxies will strip them if you try. This is also how `vetiver` works today, if I am reading it correctly, and I assume it is for similar reasons.

Unfortunately, `POST` is a bad semantic fit for model predictions. Predictions don't have side effects and are idempotent, so they are 100% safe to retry if a request fails and could theoretically be cached at any intermediate layer.

However, the HTTP specification explicitly marks `POST` requests [as non-cacheable and non-idempotent by default](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7231#section-4.3.3), which has some relevant consequences:

* Clients (like browsers) must always re-request the prediction if they need it later.
* Prediction requests cannot supply "conditional" headers like those used for `GET` requests -- e.g. `If-Modified-Since` -- that could potentially reduce a lot of computation on the server side.
* This is true for anything in between as well, e.g. reverse proxies like NGINX cannot cache `POST` requests.
* Many HTTP request libraries will quietly retry failed requests, but they won't do this for `POST` requests by default because the results could be unpredictable.

You might think that caching is unimportant, but in my experience quite a lot of prediction requests are for a small set of domain-specific "base cases".

Moreover, because `vetiver` is *generating* an API that most users probably won't customise, we'd ideally like it to be a really performant and well-behaved one out of the box.

## Proposed Feature

There is a widely-supported addition to the HTTP specification currently under review at the IETF that [will add a new `QUERY` method](https://www.ietf.org/id/draft-ietf-httpbis-safe-method-w-body-02.html):

> This specification defines the HTTP QUERY request method as a means of making a safe, idempotent request that contains content.

`QUERY` supports caching and conditional headers, and unlike `GET` the URI is not expected to represent a resource.

It's my belief that this new method is a perfect fit for usecases like model prediction, so I'd propose that we jump on this bandwagon early and support a `QUERY` endpoint for generated Plumber APIs in `vetiver`.

## Potential Issues

* Since this is a new HTTP method, it won't be widely understood by other software for a little while. But HTTP allows for arbitrary methods, so I don't think we'll actually break anything. And having the `POST` endpoint remain as a fallback would ameliorate this concern -- we could even send the new `Accept-Query` header from it.

* This new method has not been finalize by the IETF, so it's possible the specifics (though not the semantics) could change slightly in the meantime.

title: Decouple API Spec changes from `/predict` endpoint definition
description:
Currently a vetiver plumber file contains the following that defines the `/predict` endpoint:

```r
#* @plumber
function(pr) {
    pr %>% vetiver_pr_predict(v)
}
```

`vetiver_pr_predict()` does all of the heavy lifting:
* uses the appropriate handler to define the `/predict` endpoint
* re-writes the OpenAPI spec file to define the API input data and other details
* changes the docs rendering from Swagger to Rapidoc.

This proposal is to separate the endpoint definition from the OpenAPI tasks so that instead the definition might look something like the following:

```r
#* @plumber
function(pr) {
    pr %>% 
        vetiver_pr_predict(v) %>%
        vetiver_pr_openapi(v)
}
```

In this case, the user is free to define other endpoints in addition to `/predict` as well as completely remove the generated `/predict` endpoint if desired. The OpenAPI function will then inspect the router and adjust the spec file for every endpoint that identifies itself (via request method and arguments) as a model endpoint by providing requestBody definition. This way, users can define multiple model endpoints without needing to worry about defining their own spec for each endpoint.

title: Support for fairness metrics + guide to thinking more holistically about fairness
description:
As @skeydan first outlined in the prototype repo in juliasilge/deploytidymodels#3, we can prioritize a guide for choosing fairness metrics.

> In R, there is no shortage of excellent fairness metrics packages, such as https://github.com/kozodoi/fairness or, first and foremost, the bindings to AI Fairness 360 (http://aif360.mybluemix.net/).
> 
> The latter even has a document (http://aif360.mybluemix.net/resources#guidance) explaining, briefly, what usage of these metrics entails. That document, in essence, _does_ in my view convey an adequate summarization:
> 
> > If the application follows the WAE worldview, then the demographic parity metrics should be used: disparate_impact and statistical_parity_difference.  If the application follows the WYSIWYG worldview, then the equality of odds metrics should be used: average_odds_difference and average_abs_odds_difference.  Other group fairness metrics (some are often labeled equality of opportunity) lie in-between the two worldviews and may be used appropriately: false_negative_rate_ratio, false_negative_rate_difference, false_positive_rate_ratio, false_positive_rate_difference, false_discovery_rate_ratio, false_discovery_rate_difference, false_omission_rate_ratio, false_omission_rate_difference, error_rate_ratio, and error_rate_difference.
> 
> But to the user facing these questions, this may be a bit too brief. (I would assume that this brevity is also due to caution about being seen as conveying too much of an opinion.)
> 
> I'd like to suggest that in the context of _modelops_, we have a more verbose guide to assumptions underlying metrics choice, making it easier to the user to figure out what they, in fact, want to measure/assure.
> 
> As an extreme example, consider this readily-found-when-searching-the-web decision tree: http://aequitas.dssg.io/static/images/metrictree.png. From a matter-of-fact way, it is great, but since it frames its questions like so
> 
>     * do you want to ...
> 
>     * do you need to ...
> 
> 
> it does not help the user in figuring out _what_ it is they might want to do.

description:
The `ptype` concept here in vetiver is used as an **input data prototype**, for checking that the format of new data at prediction conforms to what the model had at training time.

It is already possible to totally turn off this checking, when appropriate to a certain use case.

In discussions with @t-kalinowski he explained to me how it will likely be important for keras, etc to be able to have more flexible, _partially_ defined input data shapes/prototypes such as an array that is fixed in some dimensions but could be any length in another dimension. I don't currently have great ideas for this, something flexible between "no checking" and "very strict checking".

title: Use renv to track needed packages and versions and store a hash
description:
In #2 I talk about _loading_ packages but we need to figure out how to have platforms like RSC know what packages to _install_. RSC currently uses a manifest, not renv, so we'll need to figure out some details here.

If a user has a file that looks like this:

```r
library(deploytidymodels)
library(pins)
library(plumber)

model_board <- board_rsconnect()

#* @plumber
function(pr) {
    pr %>%
        pr_model(model_board, "julia.silge/biv_svm", type = "class")
}
```

we currently will not successfully install the right packages for prediction into the app.

@topepo has already put work into creating an `renv.lock` file from a model to track what packages/versions are needed for prediction; I think this can either be used or repurposed.
